claims.quote: Servicers must comply with applicable law in connection with [their] management of escrow accounts, including collecting, holding, and escrowing funds on behalf of each borrower in accordance with RESPA (12 [U.S.C.] 2609) and Regulation X (12 CFR 1024.17 and 10024.34).
claims.summary: Servicers must comply with applicable law regarding escrow account management, including collecting, holding, and escrowing funds in accordance with RESPA and Regulation X.

claims.quote: Servicers must closely monitor property taxing authorities and individual insurance contracts to ensure that escrow calculations are accurate and that insurance policies have not lapsed.
claims.summary: Servicers must closely monitor property taxing authorities and insurance contracts to ensure accurate escrow calculations and that insurance policies have not lapsed.

claims.quote: Servicers also should ensure compliance with legal requirements regarding the cessation of escrow withholding for [private market insurance] on serviced loans.
claims.summary: Servicers should ensure compliance with legal requirements regarding the cessation of escrow withholding for private market insurance on serviced loans.

claims.quote: 12 U.S.C. 1828(o) instructs the Federal banking agencies to ``adopt uniform regulations prescribing standards for extensions of credit'' related to certain real estate transactions.
claims.summary: Federal banking agencies must adopt uniform regulations prescribing standards for extensions of credit related to certain real estate transactions.

claims.quote: 12 U.S.C. 371(a) clearly states that national banks' real estate lending powers are subject both to 12 U.S.C. 1828(o) ``and such restrictions and requirements as the Comptroller of the Currency may prescribe by regulation or order'' (emphasis added).
claims.summary: National banks' real estate lending powers are subject to both 12 U.S.C. 1828(o) and regulations prescribed by the Comptroller of the Currency.

claims.quote: A reading of the statute that section 1828(o) is the controlling basis for adopting regulations would render the Comptroller's concurrent rulemaking authority as surplusage--``[i]t is a cardinal principle of statutory construction that a statute ought, upon the whole, to be so construed that, if it can be prevented, no clause, sentence, or word shall be superfluous, void, or insignificant.''
claims.summary: The Comptroller of the Currency's concurrent rulemaking authority must not be rendered surplusage by interpreting section 1828(o) as the sole basis for adopting regulations.

claims.quote: HOLA provides Federal savings associations broad powers to invest in, sell, or otherwise deal in residential real property loans, subject to regulations issued by the Comptroller.
claims.summary: Federal savings associations have broad powers to invest in, sell, or otherwise deal in residential real property loans, subject to regulations issued by the Comptroller.

claims.quote: HOLA also provides the OCC with broad authority to prescribe rules and regulations to provide for the organization, incorporation, examination, operation, and regulation of Federal savings associations and to specify their powers to invest in, sell, or otherwise deal in various loans and other investments.
claims.summary: The OCC has broad authority to prescribe rules and regulations for the organization, incorporation, examination, operation, and regulation of Federal savings associations, as well as to specify their powers to invest in, sell, or otherwise deal in various loans and other investments.

claims.quote: HOLA also authorizes Federal savings associations to engage in nonresidential real estate lending not in excess of 400 percent of capital or certain greater amounts as determined by the Comptroller, subject to regulations issued by the Comptroller.
claims.summary: Federal savings associations are authorized to engage in nonresidential real estate lending up to 400 percent of capital or certain greater amounts as determined by the Comptroller, subject to regulations issued by the Comptroller.

claims.quote: 12 U.S.C. 1464(a); see also Fid. Fed. Sav. & Loan Ass'n v. de la Cuesta, 458 U.S. 141, 145 (1982) (``Pursuant to this authorization [12 U.S.C. 1464(a)], the [Federal Home Loan Bank] Board has promulgated regulations governing the powers and operations of every Federal savings and loan association from its cradle to its corporate grave.'' (citation modified)). This authority to promulgate regulations for Federal savings associations was ultimately transferred to the OCC. 12 U.S.C. 5412(b)(2)(B).
claims.summary: The OCC has the authority to promulgate regulations governing the powers and operations of Federal savings associations, as transferred from the Federal Home Loan Bank Board under 12 U.S.C. 5412(b)(2)(B).

claims.quote: Since the earliest days of the Federal banking system, courts have held that banks have wide latitude in managing and protecting property acquired in the usual course of banking, even where such activities are not otherwise permissible.
claims.summary: Courts have held that banks have wide latitude in managing and protecting property acquired in the usual course of banking, even where such activities are not otherwise permissible.

claims.quote: Courts have also explicitly linked the power to lend as inextricably bound up in the power to foreclose on collateral.
claims.summary: Courts have explicitly linked the power to lend as inextricably bound up in the power to foreclose on collateral.

claims.quote: mandates the provision of free annual escrow account statements,
claims.summary: Lenders must provide free annual escrow account statements.

claims.summary: Lenders must pay amounts in escrow accounts timely as they become due and return any remaining funds to the borrower after the loan is repaid.

claims.quote: establishes proportional caps on the total amounts that may be collected from borrowers in escrow accounts.
claims.summary: Lenders must establish proportional caps on the total amounts that may be collected from borrowers in escrow accounts.

claims.quote: national banks are permitted to engage in the business of banking more generally and ``all such incidental powers as shall be necessary to carry on the business of banking.''
claims.summary: National banks are permitted to engage in the business of banking more generally and all such incidental powers as shall be necessary to carry on the business of banking.

claims.quote: The exercise of the Comptroller's discretion, however, must be kept within reasonable bounds.
claims.summary: The exercise of the Comptroller's discretion must be kept within reasonable bounds.

claims.quote: The OCC considers the following factors when determining whether an activity that is not explicitly enumerated in 12 U.S.C. 24(Seventh) is nonetheless part of the business of banking:
claims.summary: The OCC considers specific factors when determining whether an activity not explicitly enumerated in 12 U.S.C. 24(Seventh) is part of the business of banking.

claims.quote: (i) Whether the activity is the functional equivalent to, or a logical outgrowth of, a recognized banking activity;
claims.summary: The OCC must consider whether the activity is the functional equivalent to, or a logical outgrowth of, a recognized banking activity.

claims.quote: (ii) Whether the activity strengthens the bank by benefiting its customers or its business;
claims.summary: The OCC must consider whether the activity strengthens the bank by benefiting its customers or its business.

claims.quote: (iii) Whether the activity involves risks similar in nature to those already assumed by banks; and
claims.summary: The OCC must consider whether the activity involves risks similar in nature to those already assumed by banks.

claims.quote: (iv) Whether the activity is authorized for State-chartered banks.
claims.summary: The OCC must consider whether the activity is authorized for State-chartered banks.

claims.quote: The weight accorded to each factor depends on the facts and circumstances of each case.
claims.summary: The weight given to each factor in determining whether an activity is incidental to the business of banking depends on the specific facts and circumstances of each case.

claims.quote: An activity is ``incidental to the business of banking if it is convenient or useful to an activity that is specifically authorized for national banks or to an activity that is otherwise part of the business of banking.''
claims.summary: An activity is considered incidental to the business of banking if it is convenient or useful to an authorized activity or part of the business of banking.

claims.quote: The OCC considers the following factors in such analysis: ``(i) Whether the activity facilitates the production or delivery of a bank's products or services, enhances the bank's ability to sell or market its products or services, or improves the effectiveness or efficiency of the bank's operations, in light of risks presented, innovations, strategies, techniques and new technologies for producing and delivering financial products and services; and (ii) Whether the activity enables the bank to use capacity acquired for its banking operations or otherwise avoid economic loss or waste.''
claims.summary: The OCC considers factors such as whether an activity facilitates the production or delivery of a bank's products or services, enhances its ability to sell or market them, or improves the effectiveness or efficiency of operations, and whether it enables the bank to use capacity acquired for banking operations or avoid economic loss or waste.

claims.quote: Flexibility to exercise a national bank's business judgment as to how to structure its escrow operations and whether and to what extent to offer any compensation to customers is a clear logical outgrowth of national banks' other powers to manage and protect collateral.
claims.summary: National banks have flexibility in structuring their escrow operations and determining the extent of compensation to offer customers, as it is a logical outgrowth of their powers to manage and protect collateral.

claims.quote: It is a fundamental precept of banking that the bank has flexibility in determining what, if any, interest is paid on the funds held in customer accounts, including escrow accounts.
claims.summary: Banks have the flexibility to determine what, if any, interest is paid on funds held in customer accounts, including escrow accounts.

claims.quote: Finally, roughly three quarters of States permit State-chartered banks flexibility to exercise their business judgment as to how to structure the financing of their escrow operations for residential real estate lending, either explicitly SSS or implicitly through silence on the subject,TTT and the OCC is not aware of any State restricting this flexibility with regards to commercial real estate lending.
claims.summary: State-chartered banks have flexibility to structure escrow operations for residential real estate lending, either explicitly or implicitly through silence.

claims.summary: A bank receiving funds in escrow pursuant to an escrow agreement executed in connection with a loan may pay interest to the borrower on those funds.

claims.quote: the final rule amends the OCC's real estate lending and appraisals regulations applicable to national banks and its lending and investment regulations applicable to Federal savings associations to add a definition of ``escrow account,'' expressly codify banks' power to establish and maintain escrow accounts, and to clarify that the terms and conditions of escrow accounts, including the extent of any compensation paid to customers, are business decisions to be made by each bank.
claims.summary: The final rule adds a definition of 'escrow account,' codifies banks' power to establish and maintain escrow accounts, and clarifies that the terms and conditions of escrow accounts, including compensation paid to customers, are business decisions to be made by each bank.

claims.quote: the final rule defines an ``escrow account'' used by national banks as an account established in connection with a loan or extension of credit secured by a lien on interest in real estate in which the borrower places funds for the purpose of assuring payment of taxes, insurance premiums, or other charges with respect to the property.
claims.summary: The final rule defines an 'escrow account' used by national banks as an account established in connection with a loan or extension of credit secured by a lien on interest in real estate in which the borrower places funds for the purpose of assuring payment of taxes, insurance premiums, or other charges with respect to the property.

claims.quote: the final rule defines ``escrow accounts'' in substantially similar terms in the context of Federal savings associations.
claims.summary: The final rule defines 'escrow accounts' in substantially similar terms in the context of Federal savings associations.

claims.quote: the final rule codifies national banks' escrow powers, including the flexibility such banks have as to how to organize and manage escrow accounts.
claims.summary: The final rule codifies national banks' escrow powers, including the flexibility such banks have as to how to organize and manage escrow accounts.

claims.quote: the final rule codifies that (1) the powers of national banks include establishing and maintaining escrow accounts in connection with real estate loans; and (2) the terms and conditions of such escrow accounts (including, but not limited to, the investment of escrowed funds, fees assessed for the provision of such accounts, and whether and to what extent interest or other compensation is calculated and paid to customers whose funds are placed in the escrow account) are business decisions to be made by each national bank in its discretion.
claims.summary: The final rule codifies that (1) the powers of national banks include establishing and maintaining escrow accounts in connection with real estate loans; and (2) the terms and conditions of such escrow accounts (including, but not limited to, the investment of escrowed funds, fees assessed for the provision of such accounts, and whether and to what extent interest or other compensation is calculated and paid to customers whose funds are placed in the escrow account) are business decisions to be made by each national bank in its discretion.

claims.quote: the final rule codifies these powers in the context of Federal savings associations in substantially similar terms.
claims.summary: The final rule codifies these powers in the context of Federal savings associations in substantially similar terms.

claims.summary: Amendments related to the collection of certified IDR entity fees and administrative fees.

claims.summary: Expand upon situations in which timeframes may be waived due to extenuating circumstances.

claims.summary: Qualified IDR items and services billed as part of a bundled payment arrangement may be submitted as part of one dispute and are subject to batched dispute rules and certified IDR entity fees for single disputes.

claims.summary: The Departments must provide a definition for a bundled arrangement in the August 2022 Technical Assistance for Certified IDR Entities.

claims.summary: The 2023 proposed rules proposed to codify the definition provided in the August 2022 Technical Assistance for Certified IDR Entities.

claims.summary: The Departments proposed to remove the language stating that bundled payment arrangements are subject to the rules for batched disputes.

claims.summary: The Departments are finalizing the amendment to remove the language stating that bundled payment arrangements are subject to the rules for batched disputes.

claims.quote: The provider shall report (or for the purpose of the Federal IDR process, the provider shall bill) the Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) code 77066 (Diagnostic mammography . . . bilateral).

claims.summary: Providers must consider services billed under a single CPT code as a bundled payment arrangement for the Federal IDR process.

claims.summary: Providers must bundle disputes using a single CPT, DRG, or HCPCS code if the dispute complies with the definition.

claims.quote: All ERAs must comply with the Accredited Standards Committee (ASC) X12 835 transaction standard adopted by HHS under 45 CFR 162.1602.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must comply with the ASC X12 835 transaction standard for electronic remittance advice (ERA).

claims.quote: The HIPAA operating rule adopted at 45 CFR 162.1603(a)(4) requires plans and issuers to use a uniform set of CARCs and RARCs for defined business scenarios.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must use a uniform set of CARCs and RARCs for defined business scenarios.

claims.quote: Any interested party can use publicly available forms to submit requests for new or modified CARCs and RARCs and accompanying explanations to the respective committees on a rolling basis.
claims.summary: Interested parties must use publicly available forms to submit requests for new or modified CARCs and RARCs and accompanying explanations to the respective committees on a rolling basis.

claims.quote: Each committee meets on a regularly scheduled, periodic basis to discuss proposed new CARCs and RARCs or modifications of existing CARCs and RARCs with the sponsors of such changes and determine whether to approve or deny the recommended change or new CARC or RARC.
claims.summary: Each committee must meet on a regularly scheduled, periodic basis to discuss proposed new CARCs and RARCs or modifications of existing CARCs and RARCs with the sponsors of such changes and determine whether to approve or deny the recommended change or new CARC or RARC.

claims.summary: Updated lists of approved CARCs and RARCs, along with an updated list of approved CARC and RARC combinations and business scenarios, must be published three times each year.

claims.quote: The RARC Committee has approved a set of specific RARCs that convey information related to the No Surprises Act, including which provisions apply to a claim, how cost sharing was calculated, and whether a payment for a claim was an initial or final payment.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers must use specific RARCs to convey information related to the No Surprises Act, including which provisions apply to a claim, how cost sharing was calculated, and whether a payment for a claim was an initial or final payment.

claims.quote: the No Surprises Act-specific RARCs do not address all required QPA disclosures or all data elements relevant to whether a payment dispute arising from an item or service included on a remittance advice is eligible for the Federal IDR process.
claims.summary: No Surprises Act-specific RARCs do not address all required QPA disclosures or all data elements relevant to whether a payment dispute arising from an item or service included on a remittance advice is eligible for the Federal IDR process.

claims.summary: Current standards and operating rules under HIPAA do not include specific requirements dictating which combinations of CARCs and RARCs must be used to communicate claim adjudication information in business scenarios anticipated by the No Surprises Act.

claims.summary: The Departments are authorized to issue regulations necessary and appropriate to carry out the provisions of chapter 100 of the Code, part 7 of ERISA, and title XXVII of the PHS Act, including establishing the Federal IDR process.

claims.summary: Plans and issuers must make disclosures regarding the QPA for providers of air ambulance services.

claims.summary: Plans and issuers must apply CARC and RARC requirements when sending remittance advice to entities without a direct or indirect contractual relationship, including for items and services not subject to the No Surprises Act.

claims.quote: These final rules do not require plans and issuers to use CARCs and RARCs on remittance advice for payments made directly to participants, beneficiaries, or enrollees--including if the remittance advice is requested by the provider that furnished the item or service for which payment is made.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers are prohibited from using CARCs and RARCs on remittance advice for payments made directly to participants, beneficiaries, or enrollees, including when the remittance advice is requested by the provider.

claims.quote: These final rules establish the general requirement that plans and issuers use CARCs and RARCs, in the manner and timeframe specified in guidance, to communicate information about whether an item or service identified on a claim is or is not subject to the surprise billing requirements under the No Surprises Act.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers are required to use CARCs and RARCs, in the manner and timeframe specified in guidance, to communicate information about whether an item or service identified on a claim is or is not subject to the surprise billing requirements under the No Surprises Act.

claims.quote: Future guidance will identify the specific CARCs and RARCs to be used in particular circumstances, which, as discussed below in section II.B.2.e of this preamble, when surprise billing protections do apply, may include use of CARCs and RARCs to communicate relevant procedural or administrative information related to application of the surprise billing protections to the items or services at issue.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers are required to use CARCs and RARCs to communicate relevant procedural or administrative information related to the application of surprise billing protections to items or services when such protections apply.

claims.quote: Future guidance will also provide any administrative and technical instructions necessary to facilitate the use of mandated CARCs and RARCs in all paper or electronic remittance advice transactions to providers that do not have a contractual relationship with the plan or issuer.

claims.quote: Commenters recommended that any guidance should include explicit timelines for compliance and provide clear direction for how specified CARCs and RARCs must be used.
claims.summary: Guidance must include explicit timelines for compliance and provide clear direction for how specified CARCs and RARCs must be used.

claims.quote: The Departments have determined that because all plans and issuers that provide ERA transactions that are subject to the HIPAA Administrative Simplification requirements are required to use CARCs and RARCs, most plans and issuers already have the capacity to implement the CARC and RARC requirement.
claims.summary: Plans and issuers that provide ERA transactions subject to HIPAA Administrative Simplification requirements are required to use CARCs and RARCs.
